title: CBSE-OSM whistleblower Sarthak Sidhant digitises 6.8 lakh PDF files of UP SIR rolls
authors: Education Desk, with inputs from PTI
shows: The Indian Express reports that Sarthak Sidhant, a student from Jharkhand, says his team read about 6.8 lakh of the Commission's Uttar Pradesh roll PDFs, most of them scans, by optical character recognition, covering the 2024 Lok Sabha roll, both rolls of the intensive revision and the 2027 draft. By his account the 15.36 crore entries were set out as 54.8 crore rows, in one table for each of the 403 constituencies, and released free on 24 November, which is the s1d labs release. The paper notes that the Commission had first put the rolls online in April mainly as scanned PDFs, and that it had not responded to the claim.
quote: his team used Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology to extract information from voter roll documents published by the Election Commission of India (ECI) for the state
The extracted data, comprising 15.36 crore entries, has reportedly been organised into 54.8 crore rows, with separate tables for each of the 403 constituencies in the state.
The ECI, however, has not yet issued any response to Sidhant's claim.
